title: Flatness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set, with a chosen element $0$, and let $(S_i,t_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms $t_{ii'}:S_i\to S_{i'}$ for $i\ge i'$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism over $S_0$, with $S_0,X_0,Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ put $X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$ and $f_i=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_{S_i}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{S_0}S$, $Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S$, $f=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is flat for some $i\ge0$.
